title: Feature Clips Now Render on GitHub, Not a Random PC | vitalii.no
description:
Writing one of these feature clips means timing frame windows against a voiceover — and timing it needs edge-tts and ffprobe on hand, which is fine in a PC session and useless for an unattended agent working from a bare container with neither tool installed.

feature-clip.yml's workflow_dispatch gained a mode input. measure builds the voice straight from the beats already committed for a feature using vo-beats.py, commits the timing back to main, and prints the beat table into the run summary in about 90 seconds, no Remotion involved. render rebuilds that same voice and fails outright if it drifts more than 6 frames from what the composition was drawn against, then renders with retries, checks the mux for a silent track, and posts a per-beat contact sheet to Telegram.

p18 (1002 frames) and p19 (982 frames) were the first two clips rendered this way end to end — composition writing still needs a paid session, but voice, render, mux, verification and publish now run as free GitHub Actions compute with the PC off.
